reviews.title: App Confuses My Members!
reviews.text:
Meetup, I have been a member and organizer of groups for quite a few years now. 

TWO big issues: putting an “offer” to join “Meetup Plus” for a ridiculous monthly amount not only is outrageous, it’s put in front of the joining page as a popup. My senior ladies who can’t afford it end up joining it accidentally…then I have to be the one to try and help them get out of it. 😡

NEXT ISSUE:
When a member opens their app, please make it open to their HOME SCREEN, not the EXPLORE screen!!!!
I get messages daily that the members can’t find their groups…they can’t sign up for anything…then they go and try joining Meetup a second time!!🙄😡🙄😡🙄

Please. I beg you. Fix that.
Most events were online. Couldn't find any events taking place in the Kissimmee area. Everything was downtown Orlando.

reviews.title: Unusable
reviews.text:
Unusable due to constant $9.99/week pop-ups

I’ve been an active Meetup user for years, but recent updates have completely ruined the experience. Now, every time I tap on an event, try to view attendee lists, or look at event photos, I’m blocked by an aggressive, full-screen pop-up demanding $9.99 a week ($169.99/year) for Meetup+. Paywalling basic social features and blurring member photos makes the app frustrating and nearly impossible to use. Charging members this much on top of what organizers already pay is absurd. Instead of encouraging people to connect, this aggressive monetization is driving long-time users like me off the platform entirely.

reviews.title: Struggling to search in this app
reviews.text: Been trying to use this app for a while now but the main issues I face with it are, the discover search is lacking - it rarely, if ever, actually gives you hits related to your search term and often doesn’t even show events that I know are happening in my area. A quick AI question suggests it’s because the app is preferentially trying to feed you new groups and new events rather than ones you might actually want to go to. Also, when trying to search through the various events in your groups/home section, it could do with more filter options so you can search by a specific date range or time of the day or whether it is free or not. These changes would make the user experience much more enjoyable and encourage me to consider actually paying for the app but for now there’s no way I’d want to put any money into it.

reviews.title: Yet another app destroyed by Bending Spoons
reviews.text:
Another fairly decent app destroyed after being acquired by Bending Spoons, one of the shadiest, most horrible tech companies (and I use the term loosely) out there.
I admit, I haven’t used it for a while but I moved to a new city and wanted to meet new friends. Only to find that my account has been removed and the app has become a subscription-based thing owned by Bending Spoons. I’m sure it’s just riddled with the worst UX possible, constant ads because the only thing they’re good at is harvesting data to sell.
Deleted with the quickness!

There is no way to appeal if they remove your group either. I bet AI does all the reviews so they don’t have to hire people, that’s how it missed something so obvious. I was thinking about creating my own group, but that is impossible. The events that are being cast on there are really nuts. I seriously don't wanna climb up a mountain and I don't wanna go on a 25 mile bike ride. 
I also don't wanna get involved in other peoples religious beliefs, and the groups that were slightly interesting to me were all online. 
I thought the principal creation of Meetup was so that you actually meet up with people in real life. 
I was on Meetup about six years ago and it was great because there were some people I got to know quite well. I left it though because my circumstances changed and I've recently come back to it and seen how awful it is now. 
To be honest I'm thinking of just deleting my profile again and joining groups on Facebook or other social sites that create events that are not so wacko... after all I don't want to end up in hospital or debate with the crazies!

reviews.title: Decayed and Terrible
reviews.text:
The Meetup app is something that I have found very useful in the past, particularly when I've been in new cities for a while.  But it is fundamentally quite a disappointment.  

The layout and discoverability of events are terrible and most of the time you are presented with far too many things that you aren't eligible for. For instance, a man may be presented with dozens of events that are for women only.  Or someone under 50 may be presented with dozens of events that are over 50s only. There is no clear way to filter or opt out of this (though of course these events soils be automatically hidden from non-eligible users).

And even more annoyingly, there are a deluge of garbage events revolving around NFTs, crypto, AI nonsense etc etc that also can't be filtered out easily without hiding more legitimate events.

Finally, new addition of a stupidly expensive subscription in order to simply message a host or see who else is going is quite frankly, disgusting.

I'm not entirely surprised that yet another app is going the way of decreasing and degrading the user experience in favour of monetization. But usually the platforms that do so are at least quite good for a little while. Whereas Meetup unfortunately has simply never met its full potential. I hope that they one day correct course.  But given that they have a near monopoly as far as I'm aware, I highly doubt that will be the case. 

That said, I'm sure there are people at Meetup that have good intentions and want to do ri

reviews.title: Feel Scammed
reviews.text:
I signed up for the free trial and found that there wasn’t much in my area for me. Either I was too old for groups, too young, or the groups I was able to join didn’t have any events happening for months. I cancelled the membership, but apparently I was a few hours too late, I had already been charged for the full year.
No problem, I’d just call and request a cancellation and refund, after all, it’s was a matter of like 3 hours. Apple denied my refund request despite Meetup having a 60 day refund window for annual accounts. This was hours.
I appealed, Apple denied again. I reached out to Meetup, they said because I paid via Apple, they could do nothing, regardless of their own policy.
Both companies said my only option is to dispute with my bank, however Apple that if I did dispute with my bank, they would lock my account. So now I am out nearly $200 for an app I cannot use, and have to go through the hassle of disputing the charge with my bank and hoping that my bank can get my money back, then disputing my locked account with Apple to be able to get my devices functional again. definitely not worth all the trouble for an app that had nothing to offer me.

reviews.title: Getting worse, not better
reviews.text: Unfortunately, Meetup’s recent updates have followed the path of many apps these days. Trying to cram in more features and different features has made it much harder to use the fundamental tasks for which it was originally designed. I use the app because I belong to a group that scheduled its activities there. That’s what I want to do when I open the app. Now I am immediately blasted with 900 other groups that they think I should be interested in. I’m not. I opened the app because I had a job to do and now I have to search for the basic task of signing up for an event. Previously, when I opened my group, I had the obvious option of seeing all the activities the group had scheduled. For some inexplicable reason, they have taken that out. Now I just get a sampling of four or five out of the dozen or more upcoming scheduled activities. Last week, I couldn’t even find an activity that I was hosting! This is a hiking club. I want to see what hikes are being offered, not just a handful that some Meetup developer thought were the most relevant hikes for me. I should not have to search to find the hikes that my subgroup is doing. Our attendance is falling off because members opening the app are not seeing the hikes being offered. If it continues, I will be lobbying to trash Meetup and find some simpler app that will let us do what we need to do.

reviews.title: Brilliant idea, terribly executed
reviews.text:
Imagine an app that helps you meet people by common interest in your local area, but that forces organizers to manually enter the postal address for every single Meetup location they ever want to set up, even in a world where Google can find a location with just a name mere seconds. 

And all that overhead and needless tedium after organizers pay nearly $350/yr of annual fee fees to do all the work of setting up fun local events for others to attend for free. That’s Meetup!  

Imagine too an app built to help you find groups that allow you not to stare at your phone… unless you’re an organizer, which is all you ever do because it’s so overly complicated to create one simple event that’s in person vs another mind-numbing Zoom. 

That’s Meetup too! 

I have no idea how a simple idea could have such a hard time finding its mojo in a world where post-pandemic people are just dying to connect to something not Zoom-based but somehow Meetup continues to do everything it can to redesign its UI over and over again without ever facing the fact that its organizers are it’s soul and its organizers have been suffering with a godawful organizing experience for over a decade or more. 

If anybody in this company that’s not a college intern hired on the cheap to revamp the mobile app sees this, for the love of god please fix your mobile app’s location bug.
